study_identification_part.si4_title: Multivariate brain-cognition associations in euthymic bipolar disorder

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Assess multivariate associations between cortical thickness abnormalities and cognitive performance (processing speed, attention, executive function) in euthymic bipolar disorder using normative modeling and canonical correlation analysis.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: HCP Young Adult; OpenBHB; OASIS-3; Cam-CAN; Newcastle University healthy adults (NCL); BLISS local healthy controls included for harmonization
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative model used large public healthy control datasets (HCP, OpenBHB, OASIS-3, Cam-CAN) and an additional Newcastle University healthy cohort; BLISS local HCs (n=26) were included during harmonization to estimate site offset.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We utilised four public datasets of T1-weighted scans from healthy controls... HCP; OpenBHB; OASIS-3; Cam-CAN... We also used a cohort of healthy adult participants scanned at Newcastle University (NCL). We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS...

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper clearly states that after quality control (removing outliers defined as residuals greater than 5 median absolute deviations, n=393), the final normative sample consisted of 5977 healthy controls. The original sample was 6344 healthy individuals, but 393 were removed during quality checking, resulting in 5977 (which is 6344-393=5951, but the paper states 5977 in Table S3, indicating this is the final analyzed sample). The paper explicitly uses n=5977 in the normative model analysis.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: A sample of n = 6344 healthy individuals were included (normative-HC: mean age 32.64; 50.3% females; see Data S1 for further details). All data were pre-processed using the standard recon-all pipeline in FreeSurfer. We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS, for each ROI by regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (i.e., site; as a random effect) on cortical thickness using a generalised additive model. The correction was performed in R using the package mgcv (https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/mgcv). We removed controls who had outliers in any ROI, defined as residuals greater than 5 median absolute deviations (n = 393).
rci2_hc_n.location: Little2024.pdf.md, page 4, lines 151-152; Table S3 in supplementary material shows n=5977

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: BD showed deficits in processing speed, attention, and executive function and exhibited abnormal cortical thickness; multivariate associations linked PS/EF performance to temporal cortical regions, though the primary CCA correlation did not reach significance.
